Necessary Packages

IBD datasets were taken from Curtis Huttenhower’s Inflammatory Bowel Disease Multi’omics Database.

Files used:

  1. ecs_3.tsv.gz (metagenomes) -> renamed ecs_3_metaG.tsv
  2. ecs_3.tsv.gz (metatranscriptomes) -> renamed ecs_3_metaT.tsv
  3. hmp2_metadata_2018-08-20.csv (metadata)
  4. host_tx_counts.csv (host transcriptome)

Sub-sampling

Need to filter to include only samples that have all four data-types: metagenomes, metatransctiptomes, and host transcriptomes.

unique(meta$data_type)

# keeping patients with the following data types 
wanted_data <- c("metagenomics", "metatranscriptomics", "host_transcriptomics")

# Filter to for relevant data types
htx <- meta %>% 
  filter(data_type == "host_transcriptomics") %>%
  dplyr::select(`Participant ID`, week_num) %>% 
  distinct()

mgx <- meta %>% 
  filter(data_type == "metagenomics") %>%
  dplyr::select(`Participant ID`, week_num) %>% 
  distinct()

mtx <- meta %>% 
  filter(data_type == "metatranscriptomics") %>%
  dplyr::select(`Participant ID`, week_num) %>% 
  distinct()

# find participant-weeks with host_transcriptomics + metagenomics + metatranscriptomics
triple_match <- htx %>%
  inner_join(mgx, by = c("Participant ID", "week_num")) %>%
  inner_join(mtx, by = c("Participant ID", "week_num"))

# Sanity checks
cat("Participants in triple_match (htx+mgx+mtx):", n_distinct(triple_match$`Participant ID`), "\n")
cat("Total matched participant-weeks:", nrow(triple_match), "\n")

# one triple-matched timepoint per participant (earliest)
chosen <- triple_match %>%
  group_by(`Participant ID`) %>%
  slice_min(week_num, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

# pull full metadata rows for all three data types at matched timepoints
final_rows <- meta %>%
  filter(data_type %in% wanted_data) %>%
  semi_join(chosen, by = c("Participant ID", "week_num"))

table(final_rows$data_type)
n_distinct(final_rows$`Participant ID`)

Directory creation

# ============================================================
# paths to  per-data-type wide TSVs
# ============================================================
data_type_files <- list(
  metagenomics         = "data/ecs_3_metaG.tsv",
  metatranscriptomics  = "data/ecs_3_metaT.tsv",
  host_transcriptomics = "data/host_tx_counts.tsv"
)

# Fixed reference files - same for every participant/week
host_genome_abundance_file <- "data/host_ko_abundance.csv"
host_genome_ko_file        <- "data/noquote_ko_host.txt"

output_root <- "participants/"

# cache paths for mapping tables 
gene_ko_map_path <- "data/cache/gene_to_ko_map.rds"
ec_ko_map_path   <- "data/cache/ec_to_ko_map.rds"

# ============================================================
# BUILD ONCE: gene symbol -> KO mapping
# ============================================================
build_gene_to_ko_map <- function(symbols, cache_path = gene_ko_map_path) {
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    return(readRDS(cache_path))
  }
  
  message("Building gene -> KO mapping (first run only)...")
  
  sym_to_entrez <- AnnotationDbi::select(
    org.Hs.eg.db,
    keys = unique(symbols),
    keytype = "SYMBOL",
    columns = "ENTREZID"
  ) %>% distinct(SYMBOL, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  links <- keggLink("ko", "hsa")  # "hsa:ENTREZID" -> "ko:K00001"
  entrez_to_ko <- tibble(
    ENTREZID = str_remove(names(links), "^hsa:"),
    KO = str_remove(links, "^ko:")
  )
  
  gene_ko_map <- sym_to_entrez %>%
    left_join(entrez_to_ko, by = "ENTREZID") %>%
    dplyr::select(SYMBOL, KO) %>%
    mutate(KO = ifelse(is.na(KO), "UNMAPPED", KO))
  
  dir.create(dirname(cache_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(gene_ko_map, cache_path)
  gene_ko_map
}

# ============================================================
# BUILD ONCE: EC number -> KO mapping
# ============================================================
build_ec_to_ko_map <- function(cache_path = ec_ko_map_path) {
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    return(readRDS(cache_path))
  }
  
  message("Building EC -> KO mapping (first run only)...")
  
  links <- keggLink("ko", "ec")  # "ec:1.1.1.1" -> "ko:K00001"
  ec_to_ko <- tibble(
    EC = str_remove(names(links), "^ec:"),
    KO = str_remove(links, "^ko:")
  )
  
  dir.create(dirname(cache_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(ec_to_ko, cache_path)
  ec_to_ko
}

# ============================================================
# Load / build both mapping tables up front
# ============================================================
# (symbols arg filled in below, after first host file is read)
ec_to_ko_map <- build_ec_to_ko_map()

# ============================================================
# Cache TSVs so each is read only once
# ============================================================
loaded_csvs <- new.env()
get_csv <- function(dtype) {
  if (is.null(loaded_csvs[[dtype]])) {
    loaded_csvs[[dtype]] <- read_tsv(data_type_files[[dtype]], show_col_types = FALSE)
  }
  loaded_csvs[[dtype]]
}

find_sample_col <- function(df, external_id) {
  matches <- names(df)[str_starts(names(df), fixed(external_id))]
  if (length(matches) == 0) return(NULL)
  matches[1]
}

# Build (or load cached) gene->KO map using the actual host file's gene list
gene_ko_map <- {
  host_preview <- get_csv("host_transcriptomics")
  build_gene_to_ko_map(host_preview[[1]])
}

# ============================================================
# Parse "EC|g__Genus.s__species" into EC + taxonomy, then
# translate EC -> KO and sum abundance for genes/ECs sharing a KO
# ============================================================
parse_ec_taxonomy <- function(feature_vec) {
  # Drop stray comment/header rows that aren't real features
  feature_vec <- feature_vec[!str_starts(feature_vec, "#")]
  
  # Split off taxonomy first (EC+description | taxonomy)
  parts <- str_split_fixed(feature_vec, "\\|", 2)
  ec_and_desc <- parts[, 1]
  taxonomy <- ifelse(parts[, 2] == "", NA_character_, parts[, 2])
  
  # Strip the ": description" suffix, keeping bare EC code
  # (leaves UNMAPPED / UNGROUPED untouched since they have no colon)
  ec_clean <- str_trim(str_remove(ec_and_desc, ":.*$"))
  
  tibble(
    EC = ec_clean,
    taxonomy = taxonomy
  )
}

write_microbe_files <- function(dtype, external_id, abundance_path, ko_path) {
  if (is.null(external_id) || is.na(external_id)) return(invisible(NULL))
  df <- get_csv(dtype)
  feature_col <- names(df)[1]
  sample_col <- find_sample_col(df, external_id)
  if (is.null(sample_col)) {
    warning(paste("No column match for", external_id, "in", dtype))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  # Drop stray header/comment rows BEFORE splitting, so abundance stays aligned
  df_clean <- df %>% dplyr::filter(!str_starts(.data[[feature_col]], "#"))
  
  parts <- str_split_fixed(df_clean[[feature_col]], "\\|", 2)
  parsed <- tibble(
    EC = str_trim(str_remove(parts[, 1], ":.*$")),
    taxonomy = ifelse(parts[, 2] == "", NA_character_, parts[, 2]),
    Abundance_RPKs = df_clean[[sample_col]]
  )
  
  translated <- parsed %>%
    dplyr::left_join(ec_to_ko_map, by = "EC") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(KO = dplyr::case_when(
      EC %in% c("UNMAPPED", "UNGROUPED") ~ EC,
      is.na(KO) ~ "UNMAPPED",
      TRUE ~ KO
    )) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(KO, taxonomy) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(Abundance_RPKs = sum(Abundance_RPKs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(Abundance_RPKs != 0) %>%           
    dplyr::select(KO, taxonomy, Abundance_RPKs)
  
  write_csv(translated, abundance_path, na = "NA")
  writeLines(unique(translated$KO), ko_path)
}

# ============================================================
# Host transcriptomics: gene symbol -> KO, summed per KO per sample
# ============================================================
write_host_files <- function(dtype, external_id, abundance_path, ko_path) {
  if (is.null(external_id) || is.na(external_id)) return(invisible(NULL))
  df <- get_csv(dtype)
  feature_col <- names(df)[1]
  sample_col <- find_sample_col(df, external_id)
  if (is.null(sample_col)) {
    warning(paste("No column match for", external_id, "in", dtype))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  translated <- df %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(feature_col), all_of(sample_col)) %>%
    rename(SYMBOL = 1, Abundance = 2) %>%
    left_join(gene_ko_map, by = "SYMBOL") %>%
    mutate(KO = ifelse(is.na(KO), "UNMAPPED", KO)) %>%
    group_by(KO) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>% 
    filter(Abundance != 0) 
  
  write_csv(translated, abundance_path, na = "NA")
  writeLines(unique(translated$KO), ko_path)
}

# ============================================================
# host_genome is fixed - copy the same reference files every time
# ============================================================
write_host_genome_files <- function(abundance_path, ko_path) {
  file.copy(host_genome_abundance_file, abundance_path, overwrite = TRUE)
  file.copy(host_genome_ko_file, ko_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}

# ============================================================
# Build one pair directory
# ============================================================
copy_pair_files <- function(microbe_dtype, microbe_ext_id, host_dtype, host_ext_id, out_dir) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  write_microbe_files(
    dtype = microbe_dtype, external_id = microbe_ext_id,
    abundance_path = file.path(out_dir, "ko_taxonomy_abundance.csv"),
    ko_path = file.path(out_dir, "noquote_ko.txt")
  )
  
  if (host_dtype == "host_genome") {
    write_host_genome_files(
      abundance_path = file.path(out_dir, "host_ko_abundance.csv"),
      ko_path = file.path(out_dir, "noquote_ko_host.txt")
    )
  } else if (!is.null(host_ext_id) && !is.na(host_ext_id)) {
    write_host_files(
      dtype = host_dtype, external_id = host_ext_id,
      abundance_path = file.path(out_dir, "host_ko_abundance.csv"),
      ko_path = file.path(out_dir, "noquote_ko_host.txt")
    )
  }
}

# ============================================================
# External ID lookups from meta
# ============================================================
get_ext_id <- function(pid, wk, dtype) {
  meta %>%
    filter(`Participant ID` == pid, week_num == wk, data_type == dtype) %>%
    pull(`External ID`) %>% 
    dplyr::first()
}

# ============================================================
# Main loop over final_rows
# ============================================================
for (i in seq_len(nrow(chosen))) {
  pid <- chosen$`Participant ID`[i]
  wk  <- chosen$week_num[i]
  base_dir <- file.path(output_root, paste0(pid, "_week", wk))
  
  mgx_id <- get_ext_id(pid, wk, "metagenomics")
  mtx_id <- get_ext_id(pid, wk, "metatranscriptomics")
  htx_id <- get_ext_id(pid, wk, "host_transcriptomics")
  
  copy_pair_files("metatranscriptomics", mtx_id, "host_transcriptomics", htx_id, file.path(base_dir, "htx_mtx"))
  copy_pair_files("metagenomics",        mgx_id, "host_transcriptomics", htx_id, file.path(base_dir, "htx_mgx"))
  copy_pair_files("metatranscriptomics", mtx_id, "host_genome",          NA,     file.path(base_dir, "hg_mtx"))
  copy_pair_files("metagenomics",        mgx_id, "host_genome",          NA,     file.path(base_dir, "hg_mgx"))
}

Running DietMicrobeNet

Created a script to benchmark memory and time for each experiment run, see run_workflow_benchmark.py script.

Experiments are defined as per sample:

  • human genome (hg) + metagenome (mgx)
  • human genome (hg) + metatranscriptome (mtx)
  • human transcriptome (htx) + metagenome (mgx)
  • human transcriptome (htx) + metatranscriptome (mtx)

Example of running benchmarking script:

# This script should be run from the run workflow directory 
python /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/run_workflow_benchmark.py \            # location of benchmark script
    --directories /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/participants/*/hg_mgx \     # sample hg+mgx
                  /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/participants/*/hg_mtx \     # sample hg+mtx
                  /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/participants/*/htx_mgx \    # sample htx+mgx
                  /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/participants/*/htx_mtx \    # sample htx+mtx
    --script /Users/burkhang/Code_Projs/DietMicrobeNet/run_workflow.py \      # location of run workflow file
    --output /Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/benchmark_results.csv \          # location of benchmark csv output
    --extra-args \                                                            # workflow arguments
        --dietmicrobehost \
        --e-weights \
        --n-weights \
        --include-orgs \
        --abundance-col "Abundance_RPKs" \
        --all-food

Read in benchmarking csv and add nodes, edges, node origins, and taxonomic information.

# ============================================================
# Parse a single network_summary.txt file into a one-row tibble
# ============================================================
parse_network_summary <- function(file_path) {
  # Default (NA) row used when the file is missing or unreadable
  empty_result <- tibble(
    n_reactions        = NA_integer_,
    n_nodes            = NA_integer_,
    n_edges            = NA_integer_,
    origin_microbe      = NA_integer_,
    origin_hostmicrobe   = NA_integer_,
    origin_none          = NA_integer_,
    origin_host          = NA_integer_,
    origin_diet          = NA_integer_,
    origin_all           = NA_integer_,
    origin_hostdiet      = NA_integer_,
    origin_microbediet   = NA_integer_
  )
  
  if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
    return(empty_result)
  }
  
  lines <- readLines(file_path, warn = FALSE)
  
  extract_number <- function(pattern, text_lines) {
    hit <- text_lines[str_detect(text_lines, pattern)]
    if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_integer_)
    as.integer(str_extract(hit[1], "\\d+"))
  }
  
  extract_origin_count <- function(category, text_lines) {
    # Matches lines like "microbe: 1069"
    pattern <- paste0("^", category, ":\\s*\\d+")
    hit <- text_lines[str_detect(text_lines, pattern)]
    if (length(hit) == 0) return(NA_integer_)
    as.integer(str_extract(hit[1], "\\d+$"))
  }
  
  tibble(
    n_reactions        = extract_number("number of reactions were found", lines),
    n_nodes            = extract_number("nodes were created", lines),
    n_edges            = extract_number("edges were created", lines),
    origin_microbe      = extract_origin_count("microbe", lines),
    origin_hostmicrobe   = extract_origin_count("hostmicrobe", lines),
    origin_none          = extract_origin_count("none", lines),
    origin_host          = extract_origin_count("host", lines),
    origin_diet          = extract_origin_count("diet", lines),
    origin_all           = extract_origin_count("all", lines),
    origin_hostdiet      = extract_origin_count("hostdiet", lines),
    origin_microbediet   = extract_origin_count("microbediet", lines)
  )
}

# ============================================================
# Count lines in a KO list file (returns NA if file missing)
# ============================================================
count_ko_lines <- function(file_path) {
  if (!file.exists(file_path)) return(NA_integer_)
  kos <- readLines(file_path, warn = FALSE)
  kos <- kos[nzchar(kos)]  # drop any blank lines
  length(kos)
}

# ============================================================
# Compute Shannon diversity from one ko_taxonomy_abundance.csv
# ============================================================
compute_shannon <- function(file_path) {
  if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
    return(tibble(shannon = NA_real_, n_taxa = NA_integer_))
  }

  df <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  # Collapse to one row per taxon: sum Abundance_RPKs across all KOs
  # assigned to that taxon, to get a per-sample taxonomic profile.
  taxon_profile <- df %>%
    group_by(taxonomy) %>%
    summarise(total_abundance = sum(Abundance_RPKs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  abund_vec <- taxon_profile$total_abundance

  tibble(
    shannon = diversity(abund_vec, index = "shannon"),
    n_taxa  = nrow(taxon_profile)
  )
}

    noquote_ko_host_path  = file.path(directory_clean, "noquote_ko_host.txt"),
    ko_tax_abund_path     = file.path(directory_clean, "ko_taxonomy_abundance.csv"),
    food_representation   = "All Foods",
    analysis_type         = "DietMicrobeHost", 
    host                  = "yes"
  )

# make sure all the columns are in the same order 
benchmark <- bind_rows(#benchmark_IBD, 
                       benchmark_DMall, benchmark_DMffq, 
                       benchmark_ZIMdm, benchmark_ZIMdmh)

# ============================================================
# Parse network summaries and bind as new columns
# ============================================================
network_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(benchmark$network_summary_path, parse_network_summary)

# ============================================================
# Compute Shannon diversity per row and bind as new columns
# ============================================================
diversity_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(benchmark$ko_tax_abund_path, compute_shannon)

benchmark <- bind_cols(benchmark, network_stats, diversity_stats)

# ============================================================
# Count KOs per row (still needs rowwise, since it uses two
# separate file paths combined into one total)
# ============================================================
benchmark_final <- benchmark %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    n_ko       = count_ko_lines(noquote_ko_path),
    n_ko_host  = count_ko_lines(noquote_ko_host_path),
    n_ko_total = sum(c(n_ko, n_ko_host), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    -directory_clean, -network_summary_path,
    -noquote_ko_path, -noquote_ko_host_path, -ko_tax_abund_path
  )

# ============================================================
# Write result
# ============================================================
write_csv(benchmark_final, output_csv_path)
df <- read_csv("benchmark_all_results_with_network_stats.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(experiment_type = factor(experiment_type, levels = experiment_order), 
         across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(., 0)), 
         source = case_when(source == "DM"        ~ "DM (dmh + all foods)", 
                            source == "DM (FFQ)"  ~ "DM (dmh + FFQ)", 
                            source == "IBD"       ~ "IBD (dmh + all foods)", 
                            source == "ZIM"       ~ "ZIM (dm + FFQ)", 
                            source == "ZIM (dmh)" ~ "ZIM (dmh + FFQ)")
  )

# sanity check 
df %>% 
  group_by(source) %>% 
  mutate(host_kos = sum(n_ko_host)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(source, host_kos, food_representation) %>% 
  distinct()

Determine how correlated potential predictors of runtime or memory are:

  • alpha diversity metrics
  • microbe KOs (not host since we only use a reference genome)
model_df <- df %>%
  select(participant_id, source, runtime_sec, peak_memory_mb, n_ko, n_taxa, shannon) %>%
  mutate(
    study = if_else(str_starts(source, "DM"), "DM", "ZIM"),
    host  = if_else(source == "ZIM (dm + FFQ)", "no", "yes"),
    diet  = if_else(source == "DM (dmh + all foods)", "all foods", "FFQ")
  )

# checking whether to use shannon or n_taxa
fit_pair <- function(response, df) {
  f_shan <- as.formula(paste0("log(", response, ") ~ shannon + log(n_ko) + study + host + diet + (1 | participant_id)"))
  f_taxa <- as.formula(paste0("log(", response, ") ~ log(n_taxa) + log(n_ko) + study + host + diet + (1 | participant_id)"))
  list(shan = lmer(f_shan, data = df, REML = FALSE),
       taxa = lmer(f_taxa, data = df, REML = FALSE))
}

mem <- fit_pair("peak_memory_mb", model_df)
run <- fit_pair("runtime_sec", model_df)

compare_performance(mem$shan, mem$taxa, metrics = c("AIC", "BIC", "R2", "RMSE")) #concerning, host effect dominates

Resource use: what to expect and what drives it

Data and methods. 104 runs from 52 participants across four input configurations. Models are linear mixed models with a random intercept per participant. Intervals are 95% profile confidence intervals.

Memory

Finding Estimate (95% CI) Where it comes from
Memory without host data, at 3,000 microbial KOs about 23.7 GB (23,657 to 23,682 MB) m_mem_host intercept (all 104 runs; KOs centered at 3,000)
Added memory for including host data +2.5 GB (+2,546 to +2,568 MB, about 11%) m_mem_host, hostyes
Added memory per extra 1,000 microbial KOs about 0.4 GB (400 to 437 MB) m_mem_host, n_ko_c
Same KO slope, host-included runs only 388 to 425 MB per 1,000 KOs m_mem_final (68 runs), n_ko_k
  • A rule of thumb: about 24 GB without host data, about 26 GB with it, plus about 0.4 GB per additional 1,000 microbial KOs. Across the 2,100 to 3,900 KOs in this benchmark, that is about 0.75 GB of spread.
  • What did not matter: number of taxa, study, and diet input. Dropping them did not worsen the model (likelihood-ratio test, \(p = 0.20\), host-included runs).
  • The two KO slopes agree (about 390 to 435 MB per 1,000 KOs), which supports the estimate.

Runtime

Finding Estimate (95% CI) Where it comes from
Added time for including host data +33 s (+12 to +54 s) m_run_final, hostyes
Time saved with the FFQ diet input vs all foods about 49 s less (21 to 77 s) m_run_final, dietFFQ
Run-to-run variation not explained by the model residual SD about 41 to 58 s m_run_final, .sigma
  • What did not matter: number of microbial KOs, number of taxa, and study. Dropping them did not worsen the model (\(p = 0.95\)).
  • Most runtime variation is unexplained. Differences between participants were small (ICC about 0.03), so run-to-run noise (cluster load, scheduling) is the likely source.
  • Where each effect comes from: the host effect is estimated by comparing runs with and without host data on the same participants (one study). The diet effect is estimated within the other study. Do not assume they add exactly in a configuration that was not tested.

Alpha diversity

Shannon diversity and the number of taxa were tested as predictors. Neither improved memory beyond the KO count, and neither predicted runtime. You do not need to compute alpha diversity to estimate resources.

Practical guidance

  1. Plan memory around two things: whether host data are included (about +2.5 GB) and the number of microbial KOs (about 0.4 GB per 1,000).
  2. Do not scale runtime requests by sample size within this range. Host data and the larger diet input add under a minute each, and run-to-run variation is similar in size.
  3. Add a margin over the point estimates. The model’s memory residual SD is about 20 to 30 MB, so a small buffer covers it. For runtime, the unexplained spread is on the order of a minute.

Limits

  • About 52 participants, with microbial inputs of about 2,000 to 4,000 KOs. Estimates should not be extrapolated to much larger inputs.
  • A single host table (12,753 KOs), so “host” means included vs not included, not a quantity of host KOs.
  • One compute environment. Runtime in particular depends on machine and load.
  • Non-significant predictors were removed, so “no effect” means no effect detectable here, and not proof of zero. For memory, the dropped terms were each under about 60 MB in the full model.

Experiment differences

Runtime and memory by experiment type

# --- RUNTIME ---
df_ibd <- df %>% filter(source == "IBD (dmh + all foods)")

# Omnibus test: is there a difference across the 4 experiment types (paired by participant)?
friedman_runtime <- df_ibd %>% friedman_test(runtime_sec ~ experiment_type | participant_id)
friedman_runtime

# Effect size (Kendall's W)
df_ibd %>% friedman_effsize(runtime_sec ~ experiment_type | participant_id)

# Post-hoc pairwise paired Wilcoxon, Holm-corrected
pwc_runtime <- df_ibd %>%
  wilcox_test(runtime_sec ~ experiment_type, paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm") %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "experiment_type")

pwc_runtime

  filter(source == "IBD (dmh + all foods)") %>% 
ggplot(aes(experiment_type, runtime_sec)) +

Network similarity: technical v biological variation

Requires graph_results.csv files under the original participants/ directory tree — not re-derived from the summary CSV used above.

# ================================================================
# read in graph_results files (aka DM[H]N output)
# GOAL: create one long format df with sample, edge, reaction, abundances
# ================================================================
participants_root <- "/Users/burkhang/Desktop/ibd_dmn/participants"

graph_files <- list.files(
  participants_root,
  pattern = "graph_results\\.csv$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

# function: get one edge information - reaction, microbe read abundance and host read abundance 
get_edge <- function(edge, df){
  cols <- paste0(edge, c("_reaction", "_h_abundance", "_m_abundance"))
  df %>%
    select(reaction = all_of(cols[1]),
           h        = all_of(cols[2]),
           m        = all_of(cols[3])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(reaction)) %>%
    distinct(reaction, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # abundance repeats across rows of same reaction
    mutate(edge = edge)
}

# function: per graph result file, get combined edge1 and edge 2 information 
combine_edges <- function(file_path){ 
  df <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = F)
  bind_rows(get_edge("edge1", df), get_edge("edge2", df))
}

# combine all graph results files from all participants
suffix <- "/output_dmh/graph/graph_results\\.csv$" # this is not unique
reactions <- tibble(file_path = graph_files) %>% 
  mutate(
    experiment_type = basename(str_remove(file_path, suffix)),
    participant_id  = basename(dirname(str_remove(file_path, suffix))),
    sample_id       = paste(participant_id, experiment_type, sep = "_"),
    data            = map(file_path, combine_edges)
  ) %>% 
  filter(!map_lgl(data, is.null)) %>%
  select(-file_path) %>%
  unnest(data) %>%
  mutate(
    h = replace_na(h, 0),
    m = replace_na(m, 0),
    feature = paste(edge, reaction, sep = "_"),   # keeps edge position distinct
    class = case_when(
      h > 0 & m > 0 ~ "shared",
      h > 0 & m == 0 ~ "host_only",
      h == 0 & m > 0 ~ "microbe_only",
      TRUE ~ "absent"
    )
  ) 

### checks
# How many samples are there 
n_distinct(reactions$sample_id)                                        # should be 68
# Count how many reactions are in each class 
reactions %>% count(experiment_type, class)                            # class depends on method
# Does a reaction ever appear on both edges?
reactions %>% count(sample_id, reaction) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow()  # most likely, yes 
# Were there any reactions with no abundances? 
sum(reactions$class == "absent", na.rm = T)                            # there should be none
# ================================================================
# create sample x reaction matrices
# GOAL: create one presence/absense matrix of reactions 
# ================================================================
reaction_full <- reactions %>%
  select(sample_id, feature, h, m) %>%
  complete(sample_id, feature, fill = list(h = 0, m = 0))   # adds missing combos as 0

# host matrix
mat_h <- reaction_full %>%
  select(sample_id, feature, h) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = h) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

# microbe matrix
mat_m <- reaction_full %>%
  select(sample_id, feature, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = m) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>%
  as.matrix()

# presence/absence: 1 if either side is above 0
mat_pa <- (mat_h > 0 | mat_m > 0) * 1

### checks
dim(mat_h); dim(mat_m); dim(mat_pa)           # should be identical: 68 x (number of reactions)
identical(dimnames(mat_h), dimnames(mat_m))   # should be TRUE

# make sure all three matrices share the same rows/cols
all_samples  <- sort(unique(reactions$sample_id))
all_features <- sort(unique(reactions$feature))

# ================================================================
# add metadata to matrix 
# GOAL: create df with metadata to match matrix row names 
# ================================================================
meta_rxns <- tibble(sample_id = all_samples) %>%
  left_join(distinct(reactions, sample_id, participant_id, experiment_type),
            by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(
    host_type    = if_else(str_starts(experiment_type, "hg_"), "genome", "transcriptome"),
    microbe_type = if_else(str_ends(experiment_type, "_mgx"), "metagenome", "metatranscriptome")
  )
stopifnot(identical(meta_rxns$sample_id, rownames(mat_pa)))
# ================================================================
# PATTERN layer - Jaccard on reaction presence
# GOAL: Does the set of reactions detected in the patterns differ systematically 
# depending on which host data type (genome vs transcriptome) and which 
# microbe data type (metagenome vs metatranscriptome) was used, 
# and does the effect of one depend on the other (interaction term)?
# ================================================================
set.seed(5)

d_jac <- vegdist(mat_pa, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)

adonis_jac <- adonis2(d_jac ~ host_type * microbe_type,
                      data = meta_rxns, 
                      strata = meta_rxns$participant_id,
                      by = "terms")
print(adonis_jac)

# are group dispersions different? (PERMANOVA can't separate location from spread)
anova(betadisper(d_jac, meta_rxns$experiment_type))
# ================================================================
# WEIGHT layer - Bray-Curtis, host and microbe sides separately
# GOAL: Among the reactions that are present, 
# does the way microbial signal is distributed across them change with the data type?
# ================================================================
set.seed(5)

# divides each sample by its total so each row sums to one 
rel_rows <- function(mat) {
  rs <- rowSums(mat)
  mat / ifelse(rs == 0, 1, rs)      # zero rows stay zero instead of NaN
}

# square root things so very abundance reactions don't dominate the distance
d_bc_m <- vegdist(rel_rows(sqrt(mat_m)), method = "bray")   # microbe side
d_bc_h <- vegdist(rel_rows(sqrt(mat_h)), method = "bray")   # host side

# NaN appears only if two samples are BOTH all-zero; check
sum(is.nan(d_bc_m)); sum(is.nan(d_bc_h))

adonis2(d_bc_m ~ host_type * microbe_type, data = meta_rxns,
        strata = meta_rxns$participant_id, by = "terms")

# host side: separate by host type, since genome weights are 1 and not RPKs
# (comparing hg and htx weights directly is not meaningful)
ids_htx <- meta_rxns$sample_id[meta_rxns$host_type == "transcriptome"]
d_bc_h_htx <- as.dist(as.matrix(d_bc_h)[ids_htx, ids_htx])
meta_htx   <- meta_rxns %>% filter(sample_id %in% ids_htx)
adonis2(d_bc_h_htx ~ microbe_type, data = meta_htx,
        strata = meta_htx$participant_id, permutations = 9999)
# ================================================================
# leave-one-participant-out (checks H4039 and everyone else)
# GOAL: there is one patient that is a known outlier 
# ================================================================
run_loo <- function(dist_obj) {
  dm <- as.matrix(dist_obj)
  map_dfr(unique(meta_rxns$participant_id), function(p) {
    keep <- meta_rxns$participant_id != p
    m <- meta_rxns[keep, ]
    r <- adonis2(as.dist(dm[keep, keep]) ~ host_type * microbe_type, data = m,
                 permutations = how(blocks = factor(m$participant_id), nperm = 999),
                 by = "terms")
    tibble(dropped = p, R2_host = r$R2[1], R2_microbe = r$R2[2], R2_interaction = r$R2[3])
  })
}

loo_jac <- run_loo(d_jac)
loo_bc  <- run_loo(d_bc_m)
loo_jac %>% arrange(desc(R2_microbe)) %>% head()
loo_bc %>% arrange(desc(R2_microbe)) %>% head()
summary(loo_jac$R2_microbe)
summary(loo_bc$R2_microbe)
# ================================================================
# TURNOVER vs NESTEDNESS (microbe side)
# GOAL: when mgx and mtx differ in which reactions they detect, is it because
#   (a) turnover:    each detects reactions the other doesn't (different reactions), or
#   (b) nestedness:  one is a subset of the other (one detects fewer reactions)?
# Jaccard dissimilarity = turnover + nestedness, so this splits the Jaccard
# result you already have into two interpretable parts.
# ================================================================

# ---- 1. microbe-side presence/absence only ----
# (mat_pa used "either side" which blends host and microbe)
pa_m <- (mat_m > 0) * 1

# ---- 2. handle empty samples ----
# An empty row (no microbe signal at all, e.g. H4039 hg_mtx) makes turnover 0/0 = NaN,
# and nestedness is trivially 1 (empty set is a subset of anything).
# So that sample can't be used in the decomposition. Drop it and report it.
empty <- rownames(pa_m)[rowSums(pa_m) == 0]
empty

keep  <- !(rownames(pa_m) %in% empty)
pa_m2 <- pa_m[keep, ]
meta2 <- meta_rxns[keep, ]
stopifnot(identical(meta2$sample_id, rownames(pa_m2)))

# ---- 3. decompose Jaccard ----
bp <- beta.pair(pa_m2, index.family = "jaccard")
# bp$beta.jtu = turnover   (replacement of reactions)
# bp$beta.jne = nestedness (difference in richness, one set contained in the other)
# bp$beta.jac = total Jaccard dissimilarity

# sanity checks: parts should add up to the total, and match vegan's Jaccard
all.equal(as.numeric(bp$beta.jac), as.numeric(bp$beta.jtu + bp$beta.jne))
all.equal(as.numeric(bp$beta.jac),
          as.numeric(vegdist(pa_m2, "jaccard", binary = TRUE)))
sum(is.nan(bp$beta.jtu)); sum(is.nan(bp$beta.jne))   # should be 0

# ================================================================
# 4. PERMANOVA on each component
# Does host_type / microbe_type shift turnover? nestedness?
# Permutations are blocked by participant, as before.
# Note: these are not Euclidean distances, so a negative SumOfSqs can
# appear (treat as ~0), as with your Jaccard interaction.
# ================================================================
set.seed(5)
perm_design <- how(blocks = factor(meta2$participant_id), nperm = 9999) # this equals strata 

test_component <- function(d, label) {
  res <- adonis2(d ~ host_type * microbe_type, data = meta2,
                 permutations = perm_design, by = "terms")
  tibble(component = label,
         term = rownames(res)[1:3],
         R2   = res$R2[1:3],
         p    = res$`Pr(>F)`[1:3])
}

component_tests <- bind_rows(
  test_component(bp$beta.jac, "total Jaccard"),
  test_component(bp$beta.jtu, "turnover"),
  test_component(bp$beta.jne, "nestedness")
)
print(component_tests)

# ================================================================
# 5. PAIRED, WITHIN-PARTICIPANT VIEW
# The PERMANOVA says whether the components shift with method.
# This says how much of each mgx-vs-mtx difference is turnover vs nestedness,
# and which direction the subset goes.
# ================================================================
jtu_m <- as.matrix(bp$beta.jtu)
jne_m <- as.matrix(bp$beta.jne)
jac_m <- as.matrix(bp$beta.jac)

# one row per participant x host_type, with the mgx and mtx sample IDs side by side
paired <- meta2 %>%
  select(participant_id, host_type, microbe_type, sample_id) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = microbe_type, values_from = sample_id) %>%
  drop_na()    # participants missing one of the two samples (e.g. the dropped one)

paired <- paired %>%
  mutate(
    jac = map2_dbl(metagenome, metatranscriptome, ~ jac_m[.x, .y]),
    jtu = map2_dbl(metagenome, metatranscriptome, ~ jtu_m[.x, .y]),
    jne = map2_dbl(metagenome, metatranscriptome, ~ jne_m[.x, .y]),
    
    n_mg = map_dbl(metagenome,        ~ sum(pa_m2[.x, ])),
    n_mt = map_dbl(metatranscriptome, ~ sum(pa_m2[.x, ])),
    
    # direction: of the reactions seen in mtx, what fraction are also seen in mgx?
    frac_mt_in_mg = map2_dbl(metagenome, metatranscriptome,
                             ~ sum(pa_m2[.x, ] & pa_m2[.y, ]) / sum(pa_m2[.y, ])),
    # and the reverse
    frac_mg_in_mt = map2_dbl(metagenome, metatranscriptome,
                             ~ sum(pa_m2[.x, ] & pa_m2[.y, ]) / sum(pa_m2[.x, ])),
    
    nest_share = jne / jac     # fraction of the difference that is nestedness
  )

paired_summary <- paired %>%
  group_by(host_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs             = n(),
    median_richness_mg  = median(n_mg),
    median_richness_mt  = median(n_mt),
    median_jtu          = median(jtu),
    median_jne          = median(jne),
    median_nest_share   = median(nest_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_mt_in_mg     = median(frac_mt_in_mg),
    median_mg_in_mt     = median(frac_mg_in_mt),
    # paired test: is nestedness larger than turnover within a participant?
    p_jne_vs_jtu        = wilcox.test(jne, jtu, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    # paired test: does mtx detect fewer reactions than mgx?
    p_richness          = wilcox.test(n_mt, n_mg, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value
  )
print(paired_summary)
# ================================================================
# Lost v kept 
# GOAL: identifying lost and kept reactinos accross methods 
# ================================================================

lost_vs_kept <- paired %>%
  mutate(
    lost_ab = map2(metagenome, metatranscriptome, function(mg, mt) {
      lost <- pa_m2[mg, ] == 1 & pa_m2[mt, ] == 0
      mat_m[mg, lost]
    }),
    kept_ab = map2(metagenome, metatranscriptome, function(mg, mt) {
      kept <- pa_m2[mg, ] == 1 & pa_m2[mt, ] == 1
      mat_m[mg, kept]
    }),
    median_lost = map_dbl(lost_ab, median),
    median_kept = map_dbl(kept_ab, median),
    # share of lost reactions that sit above the median mgx abundance for that sample
    frac_lost_above_median = map2_dbl(lost_ab, metagenome, function(l, mg) {
      ab <- mat_m[mg, pa_m2[mg, ] == 1]
      mean(l > median(ab))
    })
  )

lost_vs_kept %>%
  group_by(host_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n                  = n(),
    med_of_median_lost = median(median_lost),
    med_of_median_kept = median(median_kept),
    med_frac_above     = median(frac_lost_above_median),
    p_lost_vs_kept     = wilcox.test(median_lost, median_kept, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    p_frac_vs_half     = wilcox.test(frac_lost_above_median, mu = 0.5, exact = FALSE)$p.value
  )
# ---------- helpers ----------
perm_for <- function(m, nperm = 9999) how(blocks = factor(m$participant_id), nperm = nperm)
sub_dist <- function(d, ids) as.dist(as.matrix(d)[ids, ids])
fmt_p    <- function(p) if_else(p <= 1e-4, "p \u2264 0.0001", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.4f", p)))

run_adonis <- function(d, m, analysis, rhs = "host_type * microbe_type") {
  set.seed(5)
  res <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("d ~", rhs)), data = m,
                 permutations = perm_for(m), by = "terms")
  tibble(analysis = analysis,
         term = rownames(res), df = res$Df,
         R2 = res$R2, F = res$F, p = res$`Pr(>F)`) %>%
    filter(!term %in% c("Residual", "Total"))
}

# ---------- distances ----------
# (d_jac, d_bc_m, meta_rxns, pa_m2, meta2 already exist)
d_jac_m  <- vegdist(pa_m2, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)   # microbe-side presence
ids_keep <- meta2$sample_id                                     # drops H4039 hg_mtx (no microbe signal)
d_bc_m2  <- sub_dist(d_bc_m, ids_keep)

ids_htx  <- meta_rxns$sample_id[meta_rxns$host_type == "transcriptome"]
meta_htx <- meta_rxns %>% filter(sample_id %in% ids_htx)
d_bc_h_htx <- sub_dist(d_bc_h, ids_htx)

# ================================================================
# Testing the effect of disease status (only host = transcriptome)
# ================================================================
clin_p <- meta %>% 
  select(`Participant ID`, week_num, diagnosis) %>% 
  mutate(participant_id = paste0(`Participant ID`, "_week", week_num)) %>% 
  select(-c(`Participant ID`, week_num)) %>% 
  distinct()

one_per <- meta2 %>% 
  distinct(participant_id) %>% 
  left_join(clin_p, by = "participant_id")

one_per %>% count(diagnosis)       # cell sizes

# paired data has two rows per participant, one for each host type, but microbe-abundance stays the same
loss <- paired %>%
  filter(host_type == "transcriptome") %>%
  mutate(frac_lost = 1 - n_mt / n_mg) %>%
  left_join(clin_p, by = "participant_id")

# table
loss %>% group_by(diagnosis) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median = median(frac_lost),
            min = min(frac_lost), max = max(frac_lost), .groups = "drop")

# plot 1: paired shift
loss %>%
  pivot_longer(c(n_mg, n_mt), names_to = "microbe", values_to = "n_reactions") %>%
  mutate(microbe = case_when(microbe == "n_mg" ~ "mgx", microbe == "n_mt" ~ "mtx")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(microbe, n_reactions, group = participant_id, color = diagnosis)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2.5) + theme_bw(base_size = 13)

# plot 2: depth
depth <- tibble(sample_id = rownames(mat_m), total_m = rowSums(mat_m))
loss2 <- loss %>%
  left_join(depth, by = c("metatranscriptome" = "sample_id")) %>%
  left_join(depth, by = c("metagenome" = "sample_id"), suffix = c("_mt", "_mg"))
loss2 %>%
  pivot_longer(c(total_m_mg, total_m_mt), names_to = "method", values_to = "total_m") %>%
  mutate(method = if_else(method == "total_m_mg", "Metagenome", "Metatranscriptome")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(total_m, frac_lost, color = diagnosis)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ method, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Total microbial abundance (RPK, log scale)",
       y = "Net reduction in reactions\ndetected (1 - mtx/mgx)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13)

# one exploratory test: interaction only
# (blocked permutations are valid for this term, not for the main effect)
ids <- meta2 %>% filter(host_type == "transcriptome") %>% left_join(clin_p, by = "participant_id")
dd  <- sub_dist(d_bc_m2, ids$sample_id)
adonis2(dd ~ microbe_type * diagnosis, data = ids,
        permutations = how(blocks = factor(ids$participant_id), nperm = 9999),
        by = "terms")

# for robustness check replicate this in human reference genome
loss_hg <- paired %>%
  filter(host_type == "genome") %>%              # 16 pairs; H4039 excluded (no hg_mtx signal)
  mutate(frac_lost = 1 - n_mt / n_mg) %>%
  left_join(depth, by = c("metatranscriptome" = "sample_id")) %>%
  left_join(depth, by = c("metagenome" = "sample_id"), suffix = c("_mt", "_mg"))

cor.test(loss_hg$frac_lost, loss_hg$total_m_mt, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
cor.test(loss_hg$frac_lost, loss_hg$total_m_mg, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

Tables

# ================================================================
# Table 1: PERMANOVA
# Use the numeric version of the table, not the formatted strings,
# so gt can format p-values itself
# ================================================================
permanova_gt_data <- bind_rows(
  run_adonis(d_jac,      meta_rxns, "Pattern: presence, host + microbe side"),
  run_adonis(d_jac_m,    meta2,     "Pattern: presence, microbe side"),
  run_adonis(d_bc_m2,    meta2,     "Weight: Bray-Curtis, microbe side"),
  run_adonis(d_bc_h_htx, meta_htx,  "Weight: Bray-Curtis, host side (transcriptome only)",
             rhs = "microbe_type")
) %>%
  group_by(analysis) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(term = str_replace_all(term, c("host_type" = "Host data",
                                        "microbe_type" = "Microbe data")))

tbl_permanova <- permanova_gt_data %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "analysis", rowname_col = "term") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "PERMANOVA by data type",
    subtitle = "9,999 permutations, restricted within participant"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(df = "Df", R2 = md("R<sup>2</sup>"), F = "F",
             p = "p", p_adj = "BH-adj. p") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(R2, F), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p, p_adj), decimals = 4) %>%
  sub_small_vals(columns = c(p, p_adj), threshold = 0.0001) %>%   # shows "<0.0001"
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = c(p, p_adj), rows = p_adj < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_footnote("Negative R\u00B2 values arise from non-Euclidean distances and are treated as approximately 0.") %>%
  tab_footnote("Host-side weights are compared within transcriptome samples only (genome weights are KO counts, not RPKs).") %>%
  opt_table_font(font = "Arial")

gtsave(tbl_permanova, "tables/table1_permanova.png", vwidth = 1100, zoom = 2)

# ================================================================
# Table 2: mtx vs mgx detection and nestedness
# ================================================================
lost_summary <- lost_vs_kept %>%
  group_by(host_type) %>%
  summarise(median_abund_lost = median(median_lost),
            median_abund_kept = median(median_kept),
            pct_lost_above_median = 100 * median(frac_lost_above_median),
            .groups = "drop")

detection_table <- paired_summary %>%
  select(host_type, n_pairs, median_richness_mg, median_richness_mt,
         median_jtu, median_jne, median_nest_share, median_mt_in_mg, median_mg_in_mt) %>%
  left_join(lost_summary, by = "host_type") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

tbl_detection <- detection_table %>%
  mutate(host_type = dplyr::recode(host_type, genome = "Host genome",
                            transcriptome = "Host transcriptome")) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "host_type") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Metatranscriptome vs metagenome reaction detection",
             subtitle = "Within-participant medians") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Reactions detected",
              columns = c(median_richness_mg, median_richness_mt)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Dissimilarity components",
              columns = c(median_jtu, median_jne, median_nest_share)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Overlap",
              columns = c(median_mt_in_mg, median_mg_in_mt)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Median mgx abundance",
              columns = c(median_abund_lost, median_abund_kept)) %>%
  cols_label(
    n_pairs = "Pairs",
    median_richness_mg = "mgx", median_richness_mt = "mtx",
    median_jtu = "Turnover", median_jne = "Nestedness",
    median_nest_share = "Nestedness share",
    median_mt_in_mg = "mtx in mgx", median_mg_in_mt = "mgx in mtx",
    median_abund_lost = "Lost in mtx", median_abund_kept = "Kept in mtx",
    pct_lost_above_median = "% lost above sample median"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(median_richness_mg, median_richness_mt,
                         median_abund_lost, median_abund_kept), decimals = 0) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(median_jtu, median_jne, median_nest_share,
                         median_mt_in_mg, median_mg_in_mt), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = pct_lost_above_median, decimals = 1) %>%
  tab_footnote("H4039 hg_mtx excluded (no microbe signal), so the genome row has 16 pairs.") %>%
  opt_table_font(font = "Arial")

Figures

pcoa_panel <- function(d, m, title) {
  pc <- cmdscale(d, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
  ve <- round(100 * pc$eig / sum(pc$eig[pc$eig > 0]), 1)   # approximate for Jaccard (negative eigenvalues)

  df <- as.data.frame(pc$points) %>%
    setNames(c("PCoA1", "PCoA2")) %>%
    mutate(sample_id = rownames(pc$points)) %>%
    left_join(m, by = "sample_id")

  # per-panel PERMANOVA: microbe effect within each host type, blocked by participant
  ann <- map_dfr(c("genome", "transcriptome"), function(h) {
    ids <- m$sample_id[m$host_type == h]
    mm  <- m %>% filter(sample_id %in% ids)
    dd  <- sub_dist(d, ids)
    set.seed(5)
    r <- adonis2(dd ~ microbe_type, data = mm, permutations = perm_for(mm))
    tibble(host_type = h, label = paste0("R\u00B2 = ", round(r$R2[1], 3), ", ", fmt_p(r$`Pr(>F)`[1])))
  })

  ggplot(df, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = participant_id), color = "grey75", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(color = microbe_type), size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
    stat_ellipse(aes(color = microbe_type), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_text(data = filter(df, str_starts(participant_id, "H4039")),
              aes(label = "H4039"), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
    geom_text(data = ann, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
              hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ host_type, ncol = 1,
               labeller = labeller(host_type = c(genome = "Host genome",
                                                 transcriptome = "Host transcriptome"))) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(metagenome = "#009E73", metatranscriptome = "#CC79A7"),
                       name = "Microbial method") +
    labs(title = title,
         x = paste0("PCoA1 (", ve[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PCoA2 (", ve[2], "%)")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
}

p_pattern <- pcoa_panel(d_jac_m, meta2, "Reaction presence (Jaccard)")
p_weight  <- pcoa_panel(d_bc_m2,  meta2, "Reaction abundance (Bray-Curtis)")

fig_pcoa <- (p_pattern | p_weight) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Summary of Findings

Data setup

  • Input: one long table (reactions) with sample_id, participant_id, experiment_type, edge, reaction, h, m.
    • 68 samples (17 participants \(\times\) 4 methods).
    • 0 reactions with no signal on either side.
  • Deduplication: abundance repeats across rows of the same reaction, so keep one row per reaction per edge.
  • Features: edge_reaction, which keeps edge position distinct.
    • About 185 reactions per sample appear on both edges and are counted twice (see sensitivity checks).
  • Matrices: sample \(\times\) reaction matrices, all 68 \(\times\) 1083.
    • mat_h: host abundance.
    • mat_m: microbe abundance.
    • mat_pa: presence/absence (signal on either side).
  • Class counts: host-only, microbe-only and shared reactions per method.
    • Host type barely changes the class counts.
    • Metatranscriptome (mtx) has about half as many microbe-only reactions as metagenome (mgx): about 2,300-2,400 vs 4,500.

Why this replaces the earlier code

  • Edge sums were too coarse. Per-edge sums cannot show which reactions differ, and the motif-level Bray-Curtis compared only two independent numbers.
  • host_dominance and handoff_shift were scale artifacts.
    • Genome weights are about 280 (KO counts), versus about \(10^6\) for the transcriptome and about \(10^5\) for the microbe.
    • Do not compare them across host types.
  • edge2_*_rel was redundant (\(\text{edge2} = 1 - \text{edge1}\)).

Analysis 1: pattern (Jaccard on presence)

  • Question: does the set of detected reactions depend on host type, microbe type, or both?
  • Method: adonis2(d_jac ~ host_type * microbe_type), permutations blocked by participant, plus betadisper.
  • Results (presence on either side):
    • Microbe type: \(R^2 = 0.137\), \(p = 0.001\).
    • Host type: \(R^2 = 0.027\), \(p = 0.032\).
    • Interaction: about 0 (the small negative value is a non-Euclidean artifact).
    • betadisper: \(p = 0.24\), so these are location effects, not dispersion.
  • Results (microbe side only, H4039 hg_mtx excluded):
    • Microbe type: \(R^2 = 0.181\), \(p < 0.001\).
    • Host type: \(R^2 = 0.014\), \(p = 0.20\).
    • Interaction: about 0.
    • The earlier host effect therefore came from the host side of the reaction set.

Analysis 2: weight (Bray-Curtis on abundance)

  • Question: among present reactions, is the signal distributed differently across them by data type?
  • Method: square root (to reduce dominance of abundant reactions), row-normalize, then Bray-Curtis. Host and microbe sides are kept separate.
  • Microbe side:
    • Microbe type: \(R^2 = 0.166\), \(p = 0.001\).
    • Host type: \(R^2 = 0.009\), \(p = 0.46\).
    • Interaction: about 0.
    • The non-significant host effect on the microbe side serves as a negative control (microbial input is identical across host pairings), and behaves as expected.
  • Host side: within transcriptome (htx) samples only, since genome weights are not RPKs.
    • Microbe type: \(R^2 = 0.062\), \(p = 0.024\).
    • This probably reflects which reactions are in the graph, not changed host expression.
  • Empty rows: H4039 hg_mtx has no microbe signal.
    • After row-normalization its distance to other samples is 1.
    • The vegdist warning is expected.

Analysis 3: influence of H4039

  • Method: leave-one-participant-out PERMANOVA for Jaccard and Bray-Curtis.
  • Result: dropping H4039 raises the microbe \(R^2\).
    • Jaccard: 0.137 to 0.263.
    • Bray-Curtis: 0.166 to 0.259.
    • The next most influential participants sit at about 0.14-0.19.
    • H4039 weakens the effect, so the conclusions do not depend on it.
  • Handling:
    • H4039 hg_mtx is excluded from decomposition steps because an empty set makes turnover undefined.
    • Report it as a separate case, not as noise.

Analysis 4: turnover vs nestedness (microbe side)

  • Question: when mgx and mtx differ, do they detect different reactions (turnover) or is one a subset of the other (nestedness)?
  • Method: betapart::beta.pair, which splits Jaccard into turnover (jtu) and nestedness (jne).
    • Sanity checks pass: the parts sum to the total and match vegdist.
  • Paired results (within participant, mgx vs mtx):
    • Median richness falls from about 654 to about 450 reactions (\(p < 0.001\)).
    • Nestedness is about 0.35 and turnover about 0.025, so nestedness is about 93% of the dissimilarity.
    • About 99% of mtx reactions are also in mgx, but only about 64% of mgx reactions are in mtx.
  • Interpretation: mtx is a thinned subset of mgx, not a different set of reactions.
  • Reporting notes:
    • Do not report the negative \(R^2\) for the turnover PERMANOVA.
    • \(R^2\) is not additive across components, so compare the paired medians instead.

Analysis 5: what is lost in mtx

  • Question: are the reactions missing from mtx the low-abundance ones?
  • Results:
    • Lost reactions have a median mgx abundance of about 7. Kept reactions have about 155.
    • Only 14-15% of lost reactions are above that sample’s median abundance (50% expected if unrelated).
    • The direction is the same in all participants (16/16 genome, 17/17 transcriptome), so p-values sit at their floor.
  • Interpretation:
    • Consistent with a detection threshold: what is lost is predicted by DNA abundance.
    • This does not prove sensitivity is the only cause, since low abundance could also reflect low expression.

Analysis 6: diagnosis (exploratory)

  • Question: does the loss of reactions in mtx, or the shift in abundance profiles between mgx and mtx, differ by diagnosis?
  • Scope: descriptive only.
    • Host-transcriptome pairing, 17 participants: UC (\(n = 3\)), non-IBD (\(n = 4\)), CD (\(n = 10\)).
    • Groups are too small and uneven for inference, and nothing here is corrected for multiple comparisons.
    • Antibiotic exposure was not evaluated.
  • Results:
    • Net reduction in reactions detected (\(1 - \text{mtx}/\text{mgx}\)), median (range):
      • UC: 0.09 (\(-0.28\) to \(0.23\)).
      • Non-IBD: 0.33 (0.19 to 0.46).
      • CD: 0.41 (0.18 to 1.00).
    • The three UC values include one negative value (M2026), where the metagenome was the low-signal sample.
    • Groups differed nominally (Kruskal-Wallis \(p = 0.059\)), which is not reported further given the group sizes.
    • Host data \(\times\) microbe data interaction, blocked by participant: \(R^2 = 0.039\), \(p = 0.28\) (no evidence that the mgx-to-mtx shift in abundance profiles differs by diagnosis).
    • Diagnosis alone, mgx samples only: \(R^2 = 0.152\), \(p = 0.26\).
  • Interpretation:
    • There is no clear evidence that diagnosis changes how mtx compares with mgx, but power is very low.
    • The apparent UC difference is confounded with signal. Median mtx total microbial signal was highest in UC (about 66,000) and lower in non-IBD (about 14,000) and CD (about 11,000), and loss tracked mtx signal.
    • The UC median is also driven by a single participant (M2026).
    • These results do not support or rule out an effect of disease status on method performance.
  • Reporting notes:
    • Do not report the diagnosis main effect from the blocked PERMANOVA (\(p \approx 0.0003\)). Diagnosis is constant within participants, so within-participant permutations cannot test it.
    • Report group sizes and ranges next to any summary statistic.
    • State that CD is the largest group and the only one with a wide range, including the most extreme participant (H4039).

Analysis 7: total microbial signal (exploratory)

  • Question: does the loss of reactions in mtx depend on how much microbial signal each sample has?
  • Measure: total microbial abundance per sample (sum of microbial RPK across all reactions in the graph).
    • This is a proxy for sequencing depth and microbial fraction of the library, not depth itself.
    • Reaction loss is the net reduction in reactions detected (\(1 - \text{mtx}/\text{mgx}\)) and can be negative.
  • Scope: Spearman correlations across participants, with no multiple-testing correction.
    • Host-transcriptome pairing (primary): \(n = 17\).
    • Host-genome pairing (robustness check): \(n = 16\) (H4039 hg_mtx had no microbial signal).
    • The two pairings share the same participants and microbial samples, so the genome pairing is a check on the host input, not an independent replication.
  • Results:
    • Reaction loss vs mtx total signal:
      • Transcriptome pairing (htx_mgx v htx_mtx): \(\rho = -0.76\), \(p = 0.0004\).
      • Without H4039 and M2026: \(\rho = -0.67\), \(p = 0.006\).
      • Genome pairing (hg_mgx v hg_mtx): \(\rho = -0.72\), \(p = 0.0016\).
    • Reaction loss vs mgx total signal:
      • Transcriptome pairing: \(\rho = 0.07\), \(p = 0.80\).
      • Genome pairing: \(\rho = 0.22\), \(p = 0.42\).
    • Richness vs own total signal (transcriptome pairing):
      • mtx: \(\rho = 0.61\), \(p = 0.009\) (0.53, \(p = 0.03\) without H4039).
      • mgx: \(\rho = 0.29\), \(p = 0.25\) (0.15, \(p = 0.57\) without M2026).
    • Range of signal across participants:
      • mgx totals were narrow (about 89,000 to 228,000, median about 152,000), apart from one participant (M2026, about 900).
      • mtx totals varied about 1,600-fold (about 90 to 145,000, median about 16,700).
    • Participants with mtx totals of about 50,000 or more (5 of 17) lost 9-36% of reactions. Participants below about 11,000 (7 of 17) lost 40% or more.
  • Individual cases:
    • H4039: mtx total of about 90 and one detected reaction (99.7% lost), with an ordinary metagenome.
    • M2026: the reverse case. The metagenome was the low-signal sample (about 900 vs about 97,000 in mtx), so loss was negative (\(-0.28\)) and turnover was high.
    • In both, the sample with the least signal had the fewest reactions.
  • Interpretation:
    • Loss followed mtx signal and not mgx signal, in both host pairings.
    • Consistent with a detection limit that affects low-signal metatranscriptomes. Above a certain signal, little more was lost.
    • Loss was not zero at high signal (about 20-35% in several participants), so signal does not explain everything. This fits the roughly 14-15% of lost reactions that were above the sample’s median abundance (Analysis 5).
    • The mgx result may partly reflect its narrow range of signal, so it does not show that mgx signal is irrelevant.
  • Reporting notes:
    • Describe the measure as “total microbial signal”, not “depth”.
    • Library sizes or microbial read counts from the pipeline would be a cleaner test.
    • Report \(n\) with every correlation. Rank-based results from 16-17 participants are exploratory.
    • Diagnosis groups differ in mtx signal (Analysis 6), so signal and diagnosis cannot be separated here.
    • A practical QC suggestion from this cohort: samples with very low microbial signal should be flagged before reactions are interpreted, since absence of a reaction is weak evidence when signal is low. The cutoff (about 10,000 total RPK here) is cohort- and pipeline-specific and should not be treated as a general threshold.

Overall conclusions

  • Microbe data type is the main driver of which reactions are detected and how their abundance is distributed.
    • mtx reaction sets were almost entirely nested within mgx sets (about 99% of mtx reactions were also in mgx).
    • Differences were mostly missing reactions in mtx, not different reactions.
  • Host data type had no meaningful effect on microbial results, and there was no interaction with microbe data type.
    • The host genome supplies presence only (each KO weighted 1), so host abundance can only be compared in graphs built with the host transcriptome.
  • Reactions missing from mtx were mostly low-abundance in mgx (median about 7 vs about 155 for retained reactions).
  • Loss tracked mtx total microbial signal and not mgx signal (Spearman \(\rho = -0.76\) and \(-0.72\) in the two host pairings; \(\rho \approx 0.1\)-\(0.2\) for mgx).
    • The two lowest-signal samples (H4039 mtx, M2026 mgx) had the fewest detected reactions in that method.
    • This is consistent with a detection limit in low-signal metatranscriptomes, though it does not exclude true differences in expression.
  • Diagnosis and antibiotic exposure could not be evaluated at this sample size (\(n = 17\); UC 3, non-IBD 4, CD 10).
    • Apparent group differences in loss were confounded with total microbial signal.
